title: Three Weeks and One Short Tray
subtitle: 饮食与营养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）
meta: 主题语境：饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）　|　核心词汇：sausage　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 sausage 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1979 the baker ① cooked the sausage that no customer in the bakery would have described, and he said the cooking was the whole of the week. The ② sausage, meaning the meat itself and not the tray, ran three weeks and stayed undescribed in the book; a sausage, he said, is the only thing in a bakery that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ sausage in that bakery had the same short tray beside it, and the ④ sausage at the far oven, meaning the slice they kept for the children to taste and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A sausage, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the baker said the describing is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the sausage was the whole of the matter, meaning the share and not the meat. The ⑥ sausage, meaning the share and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; sausage, he said, is either something you cook or the only word that means both a meat and a share. He said the share is the part they remember.

By 1984 the ⑦ sausage had become a line in a bill, and the bill had become an argument about the short tray. The ⑧ sausage of the whole thing, the baker wrote in December, was one bakery and three weeks of describing; sausage, he said, is either the slice at the far oven or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ sausage I remember is the meat described in the bill, which closed in 1986 and is still described as the quietest in the bakery. A ⑩ sausage, my mother said in 1988, is the only meat that improves by being described; every sausage, she said, is a share that has agreed to look like a meat. She said the share was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 香肠（指糕饼铺里每一根旁边的那一根）
B. n. 香肠（指那根香肠本身，与薄薄的托盘相对）
C. 固定搭配：cook the sausage 煎这一根香肠
D. n. 香肠（指留给孩子们尝的那一片）
E. n. 香肠之事（抽象总称，指一处糕饼铺的香肠之事）
F. n. 香肠（指账单里写到、被描述的那一根）
G. n. 香肠、荤腥（指一件事里人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 荤腥（抽象总称，指人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: cooked the sausage that no customer in the bakery would have described
The sausage, meaning the meat itself and not the tray
the sausage at the far oven
the sausage was the whole of the matter
the sausage had become a line in a bill
The sausage of the whole thing
A sausage, my mother said in 1988

answers.why: cook the sausage 意为“煎这一根香肠”，1979 年那位面点师把糕饼铺里没有一位顾客肯描述的一根香肠做了一遍。
sausage 意为“香肠”，指那根香肠本身而不是薄薄的托盘，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被描述。
sausage 意为“香肠”，指糕饼铺里每一根旁边的那一根，每一根旁边都有同一只薄薄的托盘。
sausage 意为“香肠”，指最远那座炉口的留给孩子们尝的那一片，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
sausage 意为“香肠、荤腥”，指一件事里人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这根荤腥就是那件事的全部。
sausage 意为“荤腥”，指人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西而不是那根香肠，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
sausage 意为“香肠”，指账单里写到、被描述的那一根，到 1984 年这一根成了账单里的一行。
sausage 意为“香肠之事”，面点师十二月写道，整件事的香肠之事是一处糕饼铺和三个星期的描述。
sausage 意为“香肠”，我记得的是账单里描述过的那一根，1986 年卖完了，至今仍被说成糕饼铺里最安静的一根。
sausage 为抽象总称，母亲 1988 年说，香肠是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的香肠。
